chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Muhammad ibn Suleyman, from Sayf ibn Umeyra, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): Indeed, Allah (Mighty and Majestic) says in His Book: 'And whoever is killed unjustly, We have indeed given to his heir authority, so let him not be excessive in the killing; surely he would be aided.' So what is this excessiveness which Allah (Mighty and Majestic) has forbidden? He (peace be upon him) said: He forbade that he should kill anyone other than his killer, or dismember the killer.

I said: So what is the meaning of His words 'surely he would be aided'? He (peace be upon him) said: And which aid is greater than that the killer should be handed over to the guardians of the killed-one, so they can kill him, and there would be no follow-up consequence for him from killing him, neither in religion nor in the world.

key_terms.إِسْرَافٌ: Excessiveness or going beyond the limit
key_terms.يُمَثِّلُ: To dismember or display the body

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'excessiveness' and 'aid' in the verse of Qisas (17:33)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elucidates the boundaries of Qisas by defining 'excessiveness' (israf) as either killing a non-murderer or mutilating the body, while interpreting 'aid' (mansur) as the heir's complete immunity from further liability. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the heir's personal authority to exact retribution directly, ensuring justice is served without the need for additional compensation or legal entanglements.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Muhammad Bin Suleyman, from Sayf Bin Umeyra, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassanasws that Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying in Hisazwj Book [17:33] And do not kill any one whom Allah has Forbidden, except with the right; and whoever is killed unjustly, We have indeed Given to his heir authority, so let him not be excessive with regards to the killing; surely he would always be Aided. So what is this excessiveness which Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic has Forbidden from?’ Heasws said: ‘Forbidden that he should kill anyone other than his killer, or dismembering the killer’.

I said, ‘So what is the Meaning of Hisazwj Words surely he would always be Aided. Heasws said: ‘And which Aid is greater than that the killer should be handed over to the guardians of the killed-one, so they can kill him and there would be no follow-up (consequences) from killing him (the killer), neither in Religion nor in the world’.
